title: Normalized rational and common-stage descent of point-section transformations
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a chosen algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and all finite intermediate fields $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with their valuation rings $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizers [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, let $g:s\to s$ be any scheme automorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $\mathcal C_E^{\mathrm{int}}=D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ for the derived-complete constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], $P_E=Lg_E^*$ for completed pullback and its rational and common-stage extensions [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and $F_E^{\mathrm{int}}=\Gamma(s,-)=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. The objects $P_EK$ are again in $\mathcal C_E^{\mathrm{int}}$ [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback].

For every $E$ suppose given morphisms $\eta^E_K:F_E^{\mathrm{int}}K\to F_E^{\mathrm{int}}(P_EK)$ in $D(\mathcal O_E)$, natural for every morphism of $\mathcal C_E^{\mathrm{int}}$. For $E\subset L$, let $T_{L/E}$ be completed integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], $\alpha_K:T_{L/E}P_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}P_LT_{L/E}K$ the specified pullback comparison [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], and $\varphi_K:F_L^{\mathrm{int}}(T_{L/E}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_E^{\mathrm{int}}K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ the specified sections comparison [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Assume, under their identity and successive-extension identifications,
$$\varphi_{P_EK}F_L^{\mathrm{int}}(\alpha_K)^{-1}\eta^L_{T_{L/E}K}=(\eta^E_K\otimes1)\varphi_K.$$

On the raw rationalization $\mathcal C_E=D^b_c(s,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], set $F_E=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ with its specified action on morphism tensors, and $H_E=F_EP_E$. Then $\eta^{E,\mathrm{rat}}_K=\eta^E_K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ is natural for every morphism $u\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_E}(K,K')$, including arbitrary sums $u=\sum_jv_j\otimes a_j$, and is scalar-compatible under the rationalizations of exactly $\alpha,\varphi$ above.

More precisely, let $\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}:F_L(K\otimes_EL)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_EK\otimes_EL$ and $\bar\alpha_{E,L,K}:(P_EK)\otimes_EL\xrightarrow{\sim}P_L(K\otimes_EL)$ be those rational comparisons, and put
$$b_{E,L,K}=\bar\varphi_{E,L,P_EK}F_L(\bar\alpha_{E,L,K})^{-1}:H_L(K\otimes_EL)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_EK\otimes_EL.$$
On $D^b_c(s,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], the components at $(E,K)$ represented by $\eta^{E,\mathrm{rat}}_K$ form a natural transformation from the specified point-fiber functor to its composite with $Lg^*$, with values in the common-stage point category [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]. For a representative $u:K\otimes_EL\to K'\otimes_{E'}L$, the two functors act respectively by the classes of
$$\bar\varphi_{E',L,K'}F_L(u)\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}^{-1},\qquad b_{E',L,K'}H_L(u)b_{E,L,K}^{-1}.$$
Their naturality equation holds over this same $L$, with the component maps extended to $L$; it is preserved by further finite extension and gives the same equation for any equivalent common-stage representative. The assertion concerns arbitrary supplied integral transformations $\eta$, without prescribing their components.

source.place: Deligne, Weil II, (1.1.3), p. 150 and (1.1.7), pp. 150-151; explicit pro-etale/completed-coefficient argument extracted by Q97 from original steps 3-6 and 9 of lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural. The normalized comparison and common-stage realization assertions are agent-written, not theorems asserted by Deligne.
